topic: State: modelling a transaction life cycle as a state machine
title: The life cycle of a mobile money transaction
instructions:
## Every transaction is in exactly one state

A transfer is **Initiated** when the sender confirms it. It becomes **Pending** when sent to the provider. From Pending it is **Completed** on `provider_ok`, **Failed** on `provider_error`, or **Reversed** if the sender cancels within the window (`cancel`). A Failed transfer may be **retried** (back to Pending) at most once; after that it is final. Completed and Reversed are final.

## Do this

Write the state machine: an initial pseudo-state, the five states, every transition labelled with its event, and final states (`--> [*]`) for Completed, Reversed and Failed.
hints: Pending --> Completed : provider_ok, and similar lines for provider_error and cancel.
Failed --> Pending : retry [attempts < 1] shows the guard in square brackets; Failed --> [*] makes it final.

checks.label: Every state reachable, every transition has an event

realityNote: The State pattern implements this diagram directly: one class per state with the transitions as methods, so an illegal transition (reversing a completed transfer) cannot even be called. Payment providers publish exactly these state tables in their API documentation.
